In [[statistics]], the '''inverse Dirichlet distribution''' is a derivation of the [[matrix variate Dirichlet distribution]].  It is related to the [[inverse Wishart distribution]].

Suppose <math>U_1,\ldots,U_r</math> are <math>p\times p</math> [[positive definite matrix|positive definite matrices]] with a [[matrix variate Dirichlet distribution]], <math>\left(U_1,\ldots,U_r\right)\sim D_p\left(a_1,\ldots,a_r;a_{r+1}\right)</math>.  Then <math>X_i={U_i}^{-1},i=1,\ldots,r</math> have an inverse Dirichlet distribution, written <math>\left(X_1,\ldots,X_r\right)\sim \operatorname{ID}\left(a_1,\ldots,a_r;a_{r+1}\right)</math>.  Their joint [[probability density function]] is given by

:<math>
\left\{\beta_p\left(a_1,\ldots,a_r;a_{r+1}\right)\right\}^{-1}
\prod_{i=1}^r
\det\left(X_i\right)^{-a_i-(p+1)/2}\det\left(I_p-\sum_{i=1}^r{X_i}^{-1}\right)^{a_{r+1}-(p+1)/2}
</math>

==References==

A. K. Gupta and D. K. Nagar 1999. "Matrix variate distributions".  Chapman and Hall.
